audit.whatIsWrong: Justice Punch (E) is called a taunt in six places and Hero's Entrance (R) is called a taunt in two more. Neither taunts.
audit.why: Riot's descriptions: Justice Punch 'knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters'; Hero's Entrance 'smashes down location, knocking up nearby enemies'; Shield of Durand 'Upon releasing the charge, Galio will taunt and damage nearby enemies'. The kit flags agree - W carries hardCC and shield, E carries dash and terrain. Holding Hallowed Mist for the wrong cast is exactly the mistake this page teaches.
audit.corrected: Every 'E taunt' becomes the Justice Punch knockup; the taunt is attributed to Shield of Durand's release; Hero's Entrance is a knockup with an ally shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and phases[].side gave Gwen levels 2 and 3 and first item, contradicting whys[1], whys[2] and whys[5].
audit.why: Winds of War out-ranges Gwen's 450 cone and Galio's stacked MR eats her pre-Riftmaker damage; she only flips it at two items, which whys[6] says outright.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere despite the page's core advice being 'only commit when it is on cooldown'.
audit.why: Winds of War 11/10/9/8/7, Shield of Durand 18/17/16/15/14, Justice Punch 11/10/9/8/7 and Hero's Entrance 180/160/140 against your 22s Hallowed Mist. A 180-second ultimate at rank 1 is a genuinely long absence — that is the window to take plates in, and the page never said so.

edits.before: Galio owns these levels and I have to accept it. His Q tornado (Winds of War) out-ranges everything I have and chunks me every time I step up to farm, and I have no Mist yet to hide in — I'm just a melee with a clunky cone Q eating poke. Don't try to trade through Winds of War; last-hit at max range, take the chip, and never walk into his E (Justice Punch) dash range — that's his taunt, and it leads straight into a free trade. My passive healing keeps me topped between minions, so the goal is simply not to fall so far behind that I miss my item spike.
edits.after: Galio owns these levels and you have to accept it. Winds of War out-ranges everything you have on an 11s cooldown and chunks you every time you step up to farm, and you have no Mist yet to hide in. Do not trade through the tornado; last-hit at max range and take the chip. His step-up opens on a Colossal Smash auto reset, and the ability that actually locks you down is Shield of Durand — he charges it, then releases a taunt — while Justice Punch is a dash knockup, not a taunt. Your passive keeps you topped between minions, so just do not fall so far behind that you miss your item spike.

edits.before: Still his window, but it's about damage control now. Galio's Q poke plus his W (Shield of Durand), which reduces the damage he takes while he channels it before releasing a burst, lets him soak my snips and win any short trade I start before items — especially when he lands E (Justice Punch) to taunt me. At 6 his R (Hero's Entrance) is the real threat: he flies a roamer onto me or land-taunts me out of my own all-in, so don't overstay on a pushed wave. My one good play is reactive — bait his E taunt, drop Hallowed Mist the instant it lands so I'm untargetable while it ticks, and snip him from inside the fog. Otherwise farm, ping for jungle help, and rush Riftmaker.
edits.after: Still his window, but it is damage control now. Winds of War poke plus Shield of Durand, which cuts the damage he takes while he charges and then releases a taunt, lets him soak your snips and win any short trade before items — especially if Justice Punch knocks you up first. At 6, Hero's Entrance is the real threat: it is 180s at rank 1, so when it is gone you have a long free window, but when it is up he flies a roamer in and knocks you up out of your own all-in. Your one good play is reactive — bait the W charge, drop Hallowed Mist the instant the taunt releases so you are untargetable while it ticks, and snip him from inside the fog.

edits.before: This is where the lane flips to me. Once I have two items, Snip Snip!'s percent-max-HP magic plus its true-damage center snip cut straight through all the magic resist Galio stacks — the tankier he builds, the harder I hit, and his Q poke and W damage reduction can't out-sustain my passive healing in an extended brawl. Bait his E taunt and R, drop Mist when he commits, and grind him down inside the fog where his single-target poke can't reach me. Just respect his global R in fights elsewhere on the map — he's far more valuable to his team than to this 1v1 now.
edits.after: This is where the lane flips to you. Once you have two items, Snip Snip!'s percent-max-HP magic plus its true-damage centre snip cut straight through all the magic resist Galio stacks — the tankier he builds, the harder you hit, and his poke and W damage reduction cannot out-sustain your passive healing in an extended brawl. Bait the Shield of Durand taunt and the Justice Punch knockup, drop Mist when he commits, and grind him down inside the fog where his single-target poke cannot reach you. Respect his global R in fights elsewhere — he matters more to his team than to this 1v1 now.

notes: MAJOR CORRECTION: this page assigns Galio's taunt to the wrong two abilities, ten times over. It repeatedly calls Justice Punch (E) 'his taunt' and says Hero's Entrance (R) 'taunts you on landing'. Riot's own text: Justice Punch steps back, charges, and KNOCKS UP the first champion hit; Hero's Entrance smashes down and KNOCKS UP nearby enemies; the taunt is Shield of Durand (W), released at the end of its charge. This matters concretely - a Gwen told to 'bait his E taunt' will hold Hallowed Mist for the wrong cast and get taunted out of her mist by the W she was ignoring. Every occurrence is corrected. Second: Colossal Smash (P) is an auto-attack reset and is never mentioned. Third: the content block is first person; converted early, mid, late and the whys. Fourth: the chart gave Gwen levels 2, 3 and first item against its own whys, which say Galio owns everything up to two items; corrected to Skill/Galio/Galio/Galio/Galio/Galio/Gwen.
